title: Redeeming the firstborn
hookLine: a ceremony at thirty days for a firstborn son

lines: A FATHER, A KOHEN, FIVE COINS.
cards: A father stands at a table, holding his month-old son. Across from him stands a kohen, a man from the priestly families. Between them, five silver coins.

The kohen asks a strange question, from a set script handed down for the ceremony: which would you rather have, your firstborn son, or the five coins the Torah says you owe for him? The father, of course, chooses his son.
He hands over the coins. The kohen takes them and blesses the child. Then everyone eats.

teach.h: FROM A MONTH OLD, FIVE SHEKELS.
teach.b: Pidyon haben. Redemption of the son. First, the command.

Exodus tells Israel to set apart every firstborn to God, and then says the firstborn sons are to be redeemed. Numbers gives the terms: from a month old, the redemption price is five shekels of silver, paid to the priests.
So the ceremony waits until the baby has lived a month. Second, the reason.

teach.h: SPARED ON THE NIGHT OF THE EXODUS.
teach.b: Exodus ties it to the night of the Exodus, when the firstborn of Egypt died and the firstborn of Israel were spared. When your son asks what this means, the text says, you tell him: by strength of hand God brought us out.
A firstborn son is a living reminder of a night when firstborns were saved. Third, the replacement.
In Numbers, God takes the Levites in place of the firstborn, to serve at the sanctuary. The firstborn are released into ordinary life, and the silver marks the release.
Not every family holds the ceremony: it's for a mother's firstborn when it's a son, and families of kohanim and Levites are exempt. Fourth, the blessing.
When the coins change hands, the kohen often blesses the child with the priestly blessing from Numbers: "The LORD bless thee, and keep thee."
The question was never really about money. It's a way of saying, out loud, in front of witnesses: this child is a gift, and we know it.

how: When a mother's firstborn child is a son, many observant Jewish families hold a pidyon haben once he is a month old: the father gives a kohen five silver coins, blessings are said, and a festive meal follows.

games.q: you're the father. the kohen asks: your firstborn son, or the five coins you owe for him? what do you say?
o: my son. here are the coins.
games.why: the father chooses his son and pays the five coins; the kohen blesses the child.

practice: Bring the scene back: the table, the coins, the question, your son or the silver?

Turn it toward your own life and name one person you would never trade for anything, however the question is put, and hold their face for a few breaths. Notice when you last told them, and if you pray, give thanks for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Pidyon haben. Redemption of the firstborn son: a month old, five silver coins, a kohen's question and a blessing. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: redemption. Five coins, handed over for something no coin could buy. Rest well.
